en.headline: Hong Kong ranks second in Asia for pension systems in new index
en.dek: The city’s Mandatory Provident Fund system scored 71.2 and retained a B grade in the Marsh CFA Institute Global Pension Index, placing 16th worldwide out of 55 systems.
body: Hong Kong’s retirement system ranked second in Asia, behind only Singapore, in the latest Marsh CFA Institute Global Pension Index released on Tuesday.

The city retained its B grade, with its overall score rising slightly from 70.6 to 71.2. It placed 16th globally among the 55 systems assessed. Hong Kong scored particularly strongly on integrity, receiving an A grade of 89.4 for governance, regulation, member protection and communication.

The report noted that the Mandatory Provident Fund covers 4.97 million members. Benefits are generally accessible from age 65, and while there is no statutory retirement age in Hong Kong, most people retire between 60 and 65. The index places Hong Kong ahead of Malaysia, mainland China, Taiwan, Japan and South Korea in the Asian rankings.

Analysts said ageing populations are placing pressure on retirement systems worldwide, and the findings highlight the relative strength of Hong Kong’s framework while underscoring the need for ongoing adjustments as life expectancies rise.

zh.headline: 香港退休保障制度亞洲排名第二 僅次於新加坡
zh.dek: 本港強積金制度在Marsh CFA Institute全球退休金指數中取得71.2分，維持B級評級，在55個制度中排名全球第16。
body: 最新Marsh CFA Institute全球退休金指數周二公布，香港退休保障制度在亞洲排名第二，僅次於新加坡。
香港維持B級評級，總分由70.6微升至71.2，在全球55個受評估制度中排第16位。完整性方面表現尤其出色，在管治、規管、成員保障及資訊溝通上取得89.4分的A級評級。
報告指出，強積金涵蓋497萬名成員，福利一般可於65歲起提取。香港並無法定退休年齡，大多數人於60至65歲退休。在亞洲排名上，香港領先馬來西亞、中國內地、台灣、日本及南韓。
分析指，全球人口老化令退休制度承受壓力，有關結果顯示香港制度相對穩健，但隨着人均壽命延長，仍需持續調整。
